stories.title: Friedman’s Restaurant Ownership Buys Upper West Side Retail Space to Open New Spot
stories.excerpt: The ownership group behind famed New York City restaurants Friedman’s Restaurant and Pastrami Queen has acquired a retail co-op on Manhattan’s Upper West Side to open a new eatery, Commercial Observer has learned. The restaurant group, using the LLC Mountain View Acquisition, bought the 5,000-square-foot retail unit at 541-555 Amsterdam Avenue for $4.1 million, according to buyer representative Lee & Associates NYC. The site is currently home to Barney Greengrass, a longtime Upper West Side restaurant and fish vendor, and Hudson & Charles, a butcher shop that also sells sandwiches and groceries. Both businesses will remain in their current locations following the completion of the sale, according to Lee. The new buyer plans to open another Friedman’s Restaurant location in the retail co-op’s existing vacant unit. There are at least seven Friedman’s locations in Manhattan already, including its first-ever location at Chelsea Market. The chain offers a variety of eats and spirits, including breakfast classics, sandwiches and burgers. “The group is expanding its footprint in a top location on the Upper West Side, while also keeping a New York institution intact and operating for years to come,” Lee’s Peter Braus, who repped the buyer, said in a statement. Brandon Polakoff from Avison Young represented the seller, a family LLC doing business as 176 West 87th Leasehold. Polakoff did not immediately respond to CO’s request for comment. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Friedman's Restaurant ownership acquired 5,000-SF retail co-op at 541-555 Amsterdam Avenue, Upper West Side, for $4.1M
Expansion to seventh Manhattan location signals strong QSR demand in established residential neighborhoods
Retail ground-floor activation in mixed-use Upper West Side asset
stories.summary: The ownership group behind Friedman's Restaurant and Pastrami Queen purchased a 5,000-square-foot retail co-op on Manhattan's Upper West Side for $4.1 million to open a new Friedman's location, marking the chain's seventh Manhattan outpost. The space at 541-555 Amsterdam Avenue will remain occupied by existing tenants Barney Greengrass and Hudson & Charles during transition. This represents a retail co-op acquisition and ground-floor activation play.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance; however, sustained QSR investment and foot-traffic generation in Upper West Side retail corridors reinforce residential neighborhood quality and mixed-use appeal, supporting occupancy and rent resilience in nearby apartment buildings. Strong independent restaurant group confidence in this submarket signals stable residential demand.

stories.title: Law Firm Thompson Relocates to 4K SF at Cohen Brothers’ 622 Third Avenue
stories.excerpt: This law firm finds its new office very appealing. Thompson, a law firm that specializes in mergers and acquisitions, tax transactions, and intellectual property issues, is relocating its New York City offices to the Cohen Brothers’ 622 Third Avenue, Commercial Observer has learned. The boutique firm signed a five-year, 4,000-square-foot lease on the 16th floor of the 40-story Midtown East office tower, also known as Grand Central Plaza. Thompson will move into its new spot in the fall from its current home at 75 Broad Street in the Financial District. The asking rent was $75 per square foot, according to tenant broker Resolution Real Estate. Resolution’s Jeffrey Zund and Michael Adler represented Thompson on this deal, while Cohen Brothers was represented in-house by Marc Horowitz. Adler, Zund and Horowitz did not immediately respond to CO’s requests for comment. Designed by Emery Roth & Sons, 622 Third Avenue is between East 40th and East 41st streets and underwent a $5 million renovation in the early 2010s. Tenants in the building include employment agency TemPositions, industrial outdoor storage provider Zenith IOS, as well as commercial real estate financing and advisory firm Cooper-Horowitz. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Thompson law firm signed 5-year lease for 4,000 SF at 622 Third Avenue, Midtown East, at $75/SF asking rent
Firm relocating from Financial District; office tower undergoing stabilization within Midtown East submarketindustry.
Grade-A office leasing activity signals professional services demand in Manhattan corporate core
stories.summary: Thompson, a boutique M&A and IP law firm, leased 4,000 square feet on the 16th floor of 622 Third Avenue (Grand Central Plaza) in Midtown East for a five-year term at $75 per square foot asking rent. The firm is relocating from its Financial District headquarters at 75 Broad Street in fall 2026. The 40-story tower, owned by Cohen Brothers, underwent a $5 million renovation in the early 2010s and maintains tenants including TemPositions.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. However, continued professional services leasing in Midtown East at stable rents ($75/SF) suggests persistent office-worker density and downtown Manhattan anchoring, supporting downstream multifamily demand in adjacent residential markets (Kips Bay, Gramercy, Murray Hill) through daytime worker populations.

stories.title: Law Firm O’Melveny Renews 100K SF at 1625 Eye Street in D.C.
stories.excerpt: O’Melveny & Myers has signed a 15-year renewal for roughly 100,000 square feet at 1625 Eye Street NW in Washington, D.C., as the building’s new ownership group sets up a substantial renovation. The global law firm has been at the 405,000-square-foot building since 2003 and occupies the top three floors as its largest tenant. GreenBarn Investment Group, FarmView Ventures and capital partner Farallon Capital acquired the property in 2025. The building sits two blocks north of the White House, and includes a nine-story atrium and 425-space parking garage. “We have known this asset for many years and have always believed in the quality of the building, its irreplaceable location and its long-term potential,” John Wolf, FarmView founder and managing partner, said in a statement. The renewal comes as Washington’s office market remains divided between older properties and higher-quality buildings, and as the owners plan to reposition 1625 Eye as a higher-end workplace asset. Renovations will include a redesigned lobby, upgraded security, and retail from LDV Hospitality, including American Cut Steakhouse and an Italian café. Plans also call for a rooftop with indoor and outdoor gathering areas, a conference and event facility, and an expanded tenant fitness center. Avison Young’s Eli Barnes, Jonathan Wellborn, Will Stern, Lauryn Harris and Macy Parana represented ownership. CBRE’s Jeff Welch and JLL’s Greg McCavera and Ella Adkins represented O’Melveny. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: O'Melveny & Myers renewed 100,000 SF (15-year term) at 1625 Eye Street NW, Washington D.C., largest tenant since 2003
Building acquired by GreenBarn Investment Group, FarmView Ventures, Farallon Capital in 2025; major renovation underway
Prime office location two blocks north of White House; 405,000-SF asset with 425-space parking garage
stories.summary: Global law firm O'Melveny & Myers signed a 15-year renewal for approximately 100,000 square feet at 1625 Eye Street NW in Washington, D.C., occupying the top three floors. The building was acquired in 2025 by GreenBarn Investment Group, FarmView Ventures, and Farallon Capital, which are repositioning it as a higher-end workplace asset with substantial renovation. The 405,000-square-foot property sits two blocks north of the White House and includes a nine-story atrium and 425-space parking garage.
stories.impact: D.C. office market bifurcation (older vs. premium asset flight) supports new development of higher-quality, amenity-rich multifamily near West End/downtown corridors. Long-term anchor tenant renewal at prime location validates neighborhood investment thesis and supports residential demand from law-firm professional workforce in adjacent multifamily projects around downtown/West End D.C. submarkets.

stories.title: Clise Properties Names Benjamin Freeburg as Chief Financial Officer
stories.excerpt: Clise Properties has announced Benjamin Freeburg as its next chief financial officer. Freeburg is succeeding Bryan Joyner, who is retiring at the end of the year after 34 years with the firm. Freeburg brings more than 20 years of experience in real estate finance, including leadership roles with private and institutional investment and asset management organizations across a variety of property types. “Ben has the right background to understand capital markets, operating platforms and investment strategies to support and elevate our diverse portfolio at Clise Properties,” said Executive Chairman A.M. Clise. “We are confident his experience will provide transparent leadership and great collaboration with our internal and external partners.” Prior to Clise, Freeburg was the chief financial officer at Martin Selig Real Estate for the past two years. He previously served in leadership roles with Aegis Living and Echelon Capital, after beginning his career at BlackRock. The post Clise Properties Names Benjamin Freeburg as Chief Financial Officer appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Clise Properties (Seattle-based, multi-asset diversified platform) named Benjamin Freeburg as CFO, succeeding retiring 34-year veteran
Freeburg brings 20+ years real estate finance experience; prior CFO at Martin Selig Real Estate (2+ years) and roles at BlackRock, Aegis Living

stories.summary: Clise Properties announced Benjamin Freeburg as its next chief financial officer, succeeding Bryan Joyner after 34 years with the firm. Freeburg brings over 20 years of real estate finance and investment experience, including prior CFO roles at Martin Selig Real Estate and leadership positions with Aegis Living, Echelon Capital, and BlackRock. Freeburg's appointment underscores Clise's commitment to transparent capital markets engagement and operational collaboration.
stories.impact: Negligible direct market impact. Internal leadership succession at diversified Seattle real estate firm does not signal material changes to underwriting, capital deployment, or market positioning in multifamily or other sectors.

stories.title: Prime Finance Supplies $63M Refi for Chelsea Multifamily Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Slate Property Group has landed a $63 million loan to refinance three multifamily buildings in Manhattan’s Chelsea neighborhood, Commercial Observer has learned. Prime Finance provided the loan for Slate’s portfolio at 229 West 20th Street, 300 West 21st Street and 301 West 22nd Street, which combined feature 94 units spanning a total of 68,139 square feet. The deal closed four years after Slate secured $61.25 million of acquisition financing from Slate Asset Management (not affiliated with sponsor) for the three properties, CO first reported at the time. “The refinancing of our Chelsea portfolio reflects both the ongoing resilience of this submarket and the lasting caliber of these assets,” Martin Nussbaum, co-founder and principal of Slate Property Group, said in a statement. “Having these properties fully leased is continued affirmation of the thesis and fundamentals we built this portfolio on.” Arrow Real Estate Advisors negotiated the debt with a team consisting of Morris Betesh, Eliott Zeitoune, Alex Bailkin and Andrew Rosenberg. Slate recently renovated the three prewar buildings, including upgrading the lobbies, common areas and façades. The properties are around a half mile from the High Line and Chelsea Market. Prime Finance did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Slate Property Group secured $63M refi from Prime Finance for Chelsea multifamily portfolio: 229 West 20th, 300 West 21st, 301 West 22nd Streets
Three-building portfolio: 94 units, 68,139 SF total; fully leased; closed 4 years after $61.25M acquisition financing
Chelsea submarket demonstrates sustained resilience and asset-quality appreciation in Manhattan core
stories.summary: Slate Property Group closed a $63 million refinance loan from Prime Finance for three fully leased multifamily buildings in Manhattan's Chelsea neighborhood totaling 94 units and 68,139 square feet. The refinance comes four years after Slate's $61.25 million acquisition financing from Slate Asset Management. Strong occupancy and underlying fundamentals underscore Chelsea's continued resilience as a multifamily submarket and validate Slate's original development thesis.
stories.impact: Chelsea Manhattan multifamily refinance at favorable LTV/rate environment signals lender confidence in submarket fundamentals, stable rents, and low turnover. Full occupancy and debt layering capacity indicate robust demand from professional workers; validates pre-development feasibility and rent trajectory for new Chelsea apartment projects competing against institutional portfolios.

stories.title: Canyon Partners Provides Refi on Four-Building Elizabeth Industrial
stories.excerpt: Canyon Partners Real Estate LLC has provided a $67-million senior loan with Kurv Industrial to refinance Kurv Elizabeth, a Class-A industrial property in Elizabeth, NJ. The transaction was facilitated by CBRE. Delivered in mid-2024, Kurv Elizabeth comprises four buildings totaling more than 278,000 square feet. Designed to accommodate a variety of industrial users, the property features flexible size offerings, rear-load configurations, and upgraded LED lighting. It offers convenient access to Interstate 78 and connectivity to Lower Manhattan and Pennsylvania’s Lehigh Valley. “Kurv Elizabeth represents a compelling opportunity to finance a high-quality industrial asset in a strategically located market supported by connectivity and durable demand,” said Robin Potts, CIO of Canyon Partners. “We are pleased to build on our relationship with Kurv on this project, and we continue to see an attractive opportunity set across the industrial sector, particularly for well-located assets serving major population and logistics hubs.” The post Canyon Partners Provides Refi on Four-Building Elizabeth Industrial appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Canyon Partners provided $67M senior refi for Kurv Industrial's four-building portfolio in Elizabeth, NJ (Kurv Elizabeth)
Class-A industrial asset delivered mid-2024: 278,000+ SF, flexible configurations, I-78 access, rear-load design
Institutional capital confidence in NJ industrial logistics nodes near Manhattan and Lehigh Valley connectivity
stories.summary: Canyon Partners Real Estate provided a $67 million senior refinance for Kurv Industrial's newly delivered (mid-2024) four-building industrial portfolio in Elizabeth, New Jersey, totaling over 278,000 square feet. Kurv Elizabeth features flexible unit sizes, rear-load configurations, upgraded LED lighting, and strategic access to Interstate 78 and connectivity to Lower Manhattan and Pennsylvania's Lehigh Valley. The transaction reinforces institutional confidence in high-quality industrial assets in strategically located markets.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily nexus, but robust industrial lending in Elizabeth/NJ logistics corridor signals confidence in regional logistics growth, supporting future logistics/fulfillment employment anchors that drive regional population and multifamily demand spillover into nearby residential markets (Newark, Jersey City). Well-capitalized industrial assets near Manhattan reduce need for urban infill warehouse conversion, preserving multifamily development sites.

stories.title: ISO New England Taps Erland Construction for Holyoke Campus Expansion

The post ISO New England Taps Erland Construction for Holyoke Campus Expansion appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: ISO New England commissioned 78,500-SF all-electric, LEED-certified office building on Holyoke, MA campus via Erland Construction
Project addresses growing workforce and capacity constraints; includes training, visitor facilities, enhanced security

stories.impact: ISO New England campus expansion in Holyoke signals job growth and organizational scaling in western Massachusetts, driving near-term and medium-term regional workforce population inflow. Multifamily developers should monitor Holyoke/Springfield submarket for rising demand from ISO employee relocation and allied professional services hiring; entry point for mid-market multifamily development ahead of employer-driven demographic shift.

stories.title: Hibachi Eatery Bijin Omakase Signs 5K-SF Lease in Long Island City
stories.excerpt: A hibachi restaurant is igniting the burner in Long Island City, Queens. Bijin Omakase signed a 15-year, 5,077-square-foot lease at the base of Trio, a nine-story, 34-unit residential development owned by ZD Jasper Realty at 27-19 Thomson Avenue near where the thoroughfare meets popular Jackson Avenue, according to landlord and tenant broker RTL. Asking rent for the space was $130 per square foot. “Given the collaborative nature of our team at RTL, as soon as this space was shared internally, before it ever hit the market, I knew it would be a strong fit for our client,” RTL’s Eli Gold, who represented the tenant alongside Michael Shkreli, said in a statement. “We toured it the following day and had a fully executed lease five weeks later. It’s a true testament to understanding a client’s requirements, identifying the right opportunity before it reaches the broader marketplace, and having both sides of the table committed to getting a market deal done,” Gold added. Thomas Galo and Matthew Knispel of RTL negotiated on behalf of the landlord. The Thomson Avenue residential building has an alternative address of 27-22 44th Drive. The property’s ground-floor space met all the tenant’s needs, according to Gold. “As a hibachi concept, Bijin Omakase had very specific physical requirements, which narrowed the universe of viable spaces considerably,” Gold said. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Bijin Omakase (hibachi/omakase) signed 15-year, 5,077-SF lease at base of Trio residential building, 27-19 Thomson Avenue, Long Island City
Ground-floor retail activation in new 9-story, 34-unit residential development (ZD Jasper Realty); lease closed in 5 weeks
Hospitality tenant anchors pedestrian-level mixed-use activation in Queens residential core
stories.summary: Bijin Omakase signed a 15-year lease for 5,077 square feet at the ground floor of Trio, a nine-story, 34-unit residential development at 27-19 Thomson Avenue in Long Island City, Queens. The hibachi and omakase restaurant lease was negotiated by RTL (broker on both sides) and closed within five weeks, following rapid internal vetting. Trio is owned by ZD Jasper Realty.
stories.impact: Ground-floor food-and-beverage activation in new Long Island City residential development validates mixed-use vertical integration and supports net-lease economics for contemporary multifamily projects in Queens submarkets. QSR tenant commitment at lease close signals landlord/operator confidence in daytime and evening foot traffic from 34-unit residential base plus surrounding neighborhood, reinforcing Long Island City as a dense, urban, mixed-use submarket with strong multifamily demand elasticity.

stories.title: Inland Surpasses $1B in Seniors Housing Acquisitions
stories.excerpt: Inland Real Estate Acquisitions, LLC, negotiated and closed the purchase of two senior living communities, Deer Park Village in Deer Park, Illinois, and The Landings in Batavia, Illinois. Mark Cosenza, senior vice president of Inland Acquisitions, with assistance from Brett Smith, vice president and senior counsel of The Inland Real Estate Group, LLC, Law Department, completed the transaction on behalf of an Inland affiliate. The transaction also marks a historic milestone for Inland, with the firm now surpassing more than $1 billion in senior living acquisitions, totaling more than 20 communities in its senior living portfolio. Inland’s senior living portfolio is comprised of more than 3,100 units and more than 20 communities across Arizona, Colorado, Illinois, Kansas, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, New Jersey and Tennessee. Deer Park Village is an upscale suburban village located about 35 miles northwest of downtown Chicago. It was built in 2016 and consists of 188 units. The Landings, a 142-unit senior living community in Batavia, was constructed in 2021. The post Inland Surpasses $1B in Seniors Housing Acquisitions appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Inland Real Estate Acquisitions surpassed $1B cumulative seniors housing acquisitions (3,100+ units, 20+ communities across 9 states)
Recent closes: Deer Park Village (188 units, Deer Park, IL, built 2016) and The Landings (142 units, Batavia, IL, built 2021)
Active institutional portfolio assembly in seniors/age-restricted multifamily subsector
stories.summary: Inland Real Estate Acquisitions closed the purchases of Deer Park Village (188 units, Deer Park, Illinois, built 2016) and The Landings (142 units, Batavia, Illinois, built 2021), reaching a historic milestone of over $1 billion in cumulative seniors housing acquisitions. Inland's seniors portfolio now comprises over 3,100 units across 20+ communities in Arizona, Colorado, Illinois, Kansas, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, New Jersey, and Tennessee. The two Illinois acquisitions reinforce Midwest market depth.
stories.impact: Institutional capital consolidation in seniors housing (age-restricted multifamily) signals belief in demographic tailwinds and operational synergy economics. Inland's $1B+ platform and Midwest concentration (Illinois, Michigan focus) validate underwriting fundamentals for independent and assisted-living development in top-10 MSAs; signals rising cap-rate compression and institutional entry will elevate acquisition pricing, tightening development spreads for new senior communities in competitive Midwest markets.

stories.title: Bullish on Multifamily, Selective on Deals: Investors Navigate a More Disciplined Market
stories.excerpt: By Josh Bodin, SVP, Capital Markets Strategy & Trading and Dori Nolan, SVP, Institutional Client Engagement, Berkadia Berkadia’s second annual Mid-Year Multifamily Pulse Survey finds that investors remain confident in multifamily’s long-term outlook, even as market volatility and tighter underwriting standards are prompting greater selectivity at the individual-deal level. Conducted in June 2026, the survey drew responses from more than 100 multifamily professionals, primarily principals and directors representing private investment companies. The results point to a market where capital remains available and long-term conviction is intact, but execution standards have risen materially. The findings point to a market that remains active and constructive, even as investors apply greater discipline to individual deals. Near-term sentiment has become more cautious, but that caution has not translated into a retreat from multifamily. Instead, investors are sharpening their focus on opportunities with durable cash flow, realistic pricing, strong fundamentals, and compelling long-term value. The result is a market where capital remains available, but execution standards are higher and conviction matters more. That disconnect between sentiment and activity is also reflected in transaction data. RCA reported a 5.7% decline in apartment transaction volume in the first half of 2026 compared with the first half of 2025, while Berkadia recorded a 16.8% increase in multifamily sales volume, reaching $5.6 billion in the first half of 2026 versus $4.8 billion a year earlier. Berkadia also increased launched multifamily deal count by 5.7%, from 442 deals in the first half of 2025 to 467 in the first half of 2026, underscoring that the market is still moving even if execution has become more challenging. bullets: Berkadia's Mid-Year 2026 Multifamily Pulse Survey: 100+ respondents (principals/directors); investors bullish long-term, selective near-term
Capital remains available; underwriting standards tightened materially; focus on durable cash flow, strong fundamentals, realistic pricing
Sentiment cautious but conviction intact; disconnect between near-term caution and long-term capital deployment
stories.summary: Berkadia's second annual Mid-Year Multifamily Pulse Survey (June 2026) surveyed over 100 multifamily professionals (principals and directors) and found investors remain confident in multifamily's long-term outlook despite market volatility and tighter underwriting standards. Capital availability persists, but execution standards have risen materially. Investors are focusing on deals with durable cash flow, realistic pricing, strong fundamentals, and compelling long-term value; near-term sentiment is cautious but long-term conviction is intact.
stories.impact: Market-wide discipline tightening creates window for best-in-class, fully-entitled multifamily projects with low basis, tight underwriting, and clear lease-up paths in high-demand submarkets. Execution excellence, realistic pricing, and fundamentals-based underwriting now differentiate deal flow; rising underwriting rigor will compress risk-adjusted returns on marginal projects and favor experienced teams with proven operations and capital relationships. Regional supply pipeline tightness and sustained lender caution support strong-market acquisitions over development in softening metros.
